pt-1SD6.title: Landscape: open fields with holm and cork oaks
pt-1SD6.summary: In the southeast, open fields sparsely dotted with small Mediterranean-looking holm and cork oaks. They look dry in summer and autumn and much lusher in spring.

pt-67d6.title: Sign: stop with big font
pt-67d6.summary: Stop signs use a fairly large font. Spanish stop signs have a small, compact font.

differs.how: Spanish stop lettering is small and compact

pt-7JpO.title: Landscape: pine forest on very white sandy soil
pt-7JpO.summary: Near the coast between Setúbal and Sines, pine forests grow on extremely sandy white soil.

pt-DGfn.title: Sign: hunting sign, red and white
pt-DGfn.summary: Red-and-white hunting signs, diamond or rectangular, are common in the countryside. Spanish hunting signs are white and black.

differs.how: Spanish hunting signs are white and black

pt-FxrH.title: Route marker: coloured diagonal block on left
pt-FxrH.summary: Most kilometre markers are wide rectangles with a coloured section on the left, split diagonally from the white part. Every kilometre there is a bigger square sign with a coloured top half showing the road number.

pt-JOnQ.title: Plants: dense eucalyptus forests
pt-JOnQ.summary: Dense eucalyptus forests are mostly in the northwest.

pt-Lkpp.title: Landscape: rocky highland, striped snow poles
pt-Lkpp.summary: A rocky mountainous highland, often with yellow-and-black striped snow poles (Serra da Estrela park).

pt-MPGC.title: Plants: citrus plantations
pt-MPGC.summary: Citrus plantations are mostly along the south coast.

pt-OD5a.title: Plants: eucalyptus trees
pt-OD5a.summary: Eucalyptus is very common. The only other part of Europe where it is common is northern Spain.

pt-OZnB.title: Waystone: black and white
pt-OZnB.summary: Black and white waystones are common.

pt-Pg4g.title: Plants: maritime pine, grey-red bark, fluffy tops
pt-Pg4g.summary: Forests or plantations of maritime pine are very common in the northern half. Grey bark with red undertones, fluffy upward branches, and old trees often bare in the lower half. Also common in northern Spain.

pt-QBnA.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
pt-QBnA.summary: Black chevrons with yellow arrows. The only Mediterranean country with this colour scheme.

pt-S7ov.title: Language: street is 'Rua'
pt-S7ov.summary: The word for road is Rua. In Galicia, in northern Spain, it is spelled Rúa with an accent.

differs.how: Galicia writes Rúa with an accent

pt-Sc7E.title: Landscape: steep terraced vineyards
pt-Sc7E.summary: In the Douro wine region, east of Porto, steep terraced vineyards are common.

pt-TydI.title: Houses: square concrete blocks, white mortar
pt-TydI.summary: In the north, houses are often made of square concrete blocks joined with white mortar. Over the border in Galicia it looks similar, usually without white mortar.

differs.how: Spanish Galicia usually has no white mortar

pt-U3KE.title: Guardrail: A-type with red reflectors
pt-U3KE.summary: A-type guardrails with red reflectors. Spain's have yellow reflectors.

pt-UKlQ.title: Bollard: thin white wedge or flat, wide reflector
pt-UKlQ.summary: Either a wedge with a noticeably thin white top, or a flat post with a wide reflector. Reflectors are mostly white, sometimes orange, which is darker than Spain's yellow.

pt-Ug6C.title: Sign: road signs with white border
pt-Ug6C.summary: Road signs usually have a white border around them. Most Spanish signs do not.

differs.how: Most Spanish signs have no white border

pt-WT4U.title: Houses: decorative mosaic tiles
pt-WT4U.summary: Houses covered in decorative mosaic tiles are fairly common.

pt-WrlL.title: Language: Ç Ã Õ Â Ê, no Ñ
pt-WrlL.summary: A Romance language close to Spanish, with the letters Ç, Ã, Õ, Â and Ê but no Ñ. Ç is also used in Catalan.

differs.how: Spanish has Ñ and lacks Ã and Õ

pt-X5pr.title: Landscape: flat, dry, almost treeless
pt-X5pr.summary: In the far southwest, flat uncultivated land that looks dry, with almost no trees and only low bushes and grass.

pt-aXLK.title: Direction sign: white, black arrows off the edge
pt-aXLK.summary: White signs with black arrows that do not touch the sign's border. Spanish signs show road numbers in coloured boxes and have no black arrow, only a thin black border.

differs.how: Spanish signs use coloured road-number boxes, no black arrow

pt-az-159s.title: Street sign: painted ceramic tile, blue letters
pt-az-159s.summary: Street signs are almost always painted ceramic tiles with blue letters and usually a decorative edge.

pt-az-2fiy.title: Coverage: walking trekker along a crater rim
pt-az-2fiy.summary: A trekker walking along a crater edge on Faial.

pt-az-2vH0.title: Plants: Japanese cedar
pt-az-2vH0.summary: Japanese cedars are very common on the Azores. They are less common on Madeira and not native to mainland Europe.

pt-az-6R9V.title: Landscape: rolling fields, round hills behind
pt-az-6R9V.summary: Most Azores coverage shows open farm fields in rolling land, often with taller round hills behind. Madeira is very mountainous and rarely has open fields.

pt-az-D5Ni.title: Houses: low, white or pastel, grey trim
pt-az-D5Ni.summary: Houses are one or two storeys with orange tiled roofs, painted white or pastel, often with dark green shutters. Yellow or blue trim is like the mainland, but grey trim is almost only on the Azores.

pt-az-HWk5.title: Wall: whitewashed with dark basalt stones
pt-az-HWk5.summary: On Faial you sometimes see traditional whitewashed rock walls with unevenly sized dark basalt stones.

pt-az-Lvxy.title: Landscape: lakes on an island
pt-az-Lvxy.summary: São Miguel is the only island in the Azores or Madeira with lakes.

pt-az-MSfT.title: Wall: dry rock walls of volcanic stone
pt-az-MSfT.summary: Dry walls of volcanic rock are very common on the Azores. They are rare on Madeira, and mainland ones are not volcanic.

pt-az-Ukps.title: Wall: rock wall with white painted concrete top
pt-az-Ukps.summary: Rock walls topped with white-painted concrete are fairly common on Terceira.

pt-az-eaE2.title: Animals: black and white cows
pt-az-eaE2.summary: Black and white cows are very common on the Azores. On Madeira cows are usually brown with white spots.

pt-az-fva4.title: Pole: mainland-style infrastructure on islands
pt-az-fva4.summary: The Azores are an autonomous region, so poles, chevrons and bollards look like those on the mainland.

pt-az-j5G7.title: Coverage: Gen 4 on only one island
pt-az-j5G7.summary: Only São Miguel has Gen 4 coverage.

pt-az-lyKf.title: Coverage: car coverage on only three islands
pt-az-lyKf.summary: Only São Miguel, Terceira and Faial have car coverage.

pt-az-rdxB.title: Direction sign: striped signpost
pt-az-rdxB.summary: Signposts are often striped, as on Madeira.

pt-az-uDZd.title: Plants: hydrangeas
pt-az-uDZd.summary: Hydrangeas are common on the Azores and rarely seen on Madeira.

pt-az-yWA1.title: Coverage: low-quality camera, dented or smooth car
pt-az-yWA1.summary: The low-quality camera is on São Miguel and Faial. On São Miguel the car has a dent in the middle; on Faial it looks smooth, sometimes with an antenna.

pt-csJJ.title: Houses: decorative chimneys, round or square
pt-csJJ.summary: In the southern Faro district, decorative chimneys are very common, round or square with small spire tops. The round ones are a strong clue.

pt-eha3.title: Houses: blue or yellow paint lines
pt-eha3.summary: Blue or yellow lines are painted around windows, doors and wall edges.

pt-fbSP.title: Pole: concrete ladder pole, tall steps
pt-fbSP.summary: Concrete ladder poles with very tall steps, often with a small see-through hole in each step. Spain and France have ladder poles with short steps.

differs.how: Spanish ladder poles have short steps
French ladder poles have short steps

pt-gIlH.title: Street sign: lime green
pt-gIlH.summary: Lime green street signs are found in Porto.

pt-kEDt.title: Houses: white stone, orange tiled roof
pt-kEDt.summary: White-painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common.

pt-lhWL.title: Plate: long white, blue left, yellow right
pt-lhWL.summary: Long white plates with a blue strip on the left and, on most, a yellow strip on the right, which is unique. The yellow strip stopped in 2020, so Gen 4 may show plates with only the blue strip.

pt-lm-2241.title: Language: street words, Rua and avenida
pt-lm-2241.summary: Rua is street. Other words: avenida (avenue), calçada (path), autoestrada (motorway), estrada (road). Spanish Galicia writes Rúa.

pt-lm-2242.hide: no learnable content (single example word, covered by pt-lm-2243)

pt-lm-2243.title: Language: ã, -ção, nh, lh endings
pt-lm-2243.summary: Look for ã and words ending in -ção, -dade, -ismo or -mente. Common words: não, são, com, por, que. Digraphs nh and lh. Spanish and Portuguese share many words, including PARE for stop in South America.

pt-lm-2979.title: Pedestrian: white belt, bent knees
pt-lm-2979.summary: A pedestrian figure with a white belt, flat shoes and bent knees. The bent knees are unique; the belt is shared with Croatia/Bosnia, Germany and Hungary.

differs.how: German figure lacks the bent knees
Hungarian figure lacks the bent knees

pt-lm-783119.title: Language: nh, lh and da/do word contractions
pt-lm-783119.summary: Portuguese uses -ao endings and nh instead of ñ, plus lh. Spanish de and del are often contracted to da, do, das and dos. Ñ only exists in Spanish; Ç, Ã, Õ, Â, Ê only in Portuguese.

differs.how: Spanish has Ñ and del instead of do/da

pt-mTk9.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
pt-mTk9.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it easy to miss.

pt-ma-06MA.title: Landscape: terraced farms with stone walls
pt-ma-06MA.summary: With so little flat land, terrace farming is widespread, with stone walls between the plateaus.

pt-ma-18cP.title: Guardrail: yellow and black
pt-ma-18cP.summary: Yellow-and-black guardrails sometimes appear on mountain roads.

pt-ma-2DE7.title: Landscape: jagged vertical sea stacks
pt-ma-2DE7.summary: The islets of Ribeira de Janela in the northwest are a famous photo spot with a vertical, jagged shape.

pt-ma-4VKJ.title: Sign: loose cows warning, brown with white
pt-ma-4VKJ.summary: On high roads you can find free-roaming cows and warning signs for them. They are usually brown with white spots, unlike the black and white cows of the Azores.

pt-ma-5Kfy.title: Landscape: 100 m waterfall onto the road
pt-ma-5Kfy.summary: Cascata dos Anjos in the southwest is a 100-metre waterfall that falls onto the road.

pt-ma-6mIy.title: Airport: built on many concrete pillars
pt-ma-6mIy.summary: The airport in eastern Madeira is built on many concrete pillars on its north side.

pt-ma-7hDE.title: Landscape: flat misty plateau, wind turbines
pt-ma-7hDE.summary: The centre-west has an elevated plateau that is unusually flat, misty, with wind turbines.

pt-ma-8zkm.title: Landscape: dark sharp rocks, island behind
pt-ma-8zkm.summary: Dark, sharp rock formations with an island in the background are in Porto Moniz, in the northwest.

pt-ma-BGSE.title: Guardrail: black-and-yellow below odd mountains
pt-ma-BGSE.summary: The road east of the plateau has unique mountain shapes and a black-and-yellow guardrail.

pt-ma-CWY3.title: Houses: white, grey or pastel, tidy red roofs
pt-ma-CWY3.summary: Houses are mainly white, grey or pastel yellow and pink, and the red tile roofs are often in good condition.

pt-ma-CXPS.title: Bollard: small stone, red reflector
pt-ma-CXPS.summary: Small, unique stone bollards with a red reflector, either box-shaped or round.

pt-ma-FT2D.title: Plants: occasional hydrangeas
pt-ma-FT2D.summary: Hydrangeas appear occasionally on Madeira but are more common on the Azores.

pt-ma-Fnoy.title: Plants: eucalyptus forests
pt-ma-Fnoy.summary: Madeira has lots of eucalyptus forest that can look like the mainland. The Azores rarely have eucalyptus.

pt-ma-Hntd.title: Landscape: lone rock on a raised hill
pt-ma-Hntd.summary: Penha d'Águia, in the northeast, stands isolated on a raised hill.

pt-ma-J3BX.title: Plants: African lily, blue or white flowers
pt-ma-J3BX.summary: African lilies are very common: long grassy leaves and round flower clusters on a tall stem, most often white or blue.

pt-ma-KKWQ.title: Landscape: high peak, white radar station
pt-ma-KKWQ.summary: Pico Areeiro, the second highest mountain and highest with coverage, has a view over most of the island and a white radar station at the top.

pt-ma-KlHM.title: Landscape: very mountainous, semi-tropical island
pt-ma-KlHM.summary: Madeira is very mountainous and semi-tropical. The Azores are less mountainous and cooler.

pt-ma-MaYa.title: Road: dark tarmac, brownish bare soil
pt-ma-MaYa.summary: Road ER211 has dark pavement and exposed brownish soil.

pt-ma-PUaV.title: Coverage: gloomy low-quality camera, white car
pt-ma-PUaV.summary: A low-quality camera with a wide round car blur that makes images look gloomy. You often see the unblurred back of a white car. Good maps usually exclude it.

pt-ma-Pezj.title: Landscape: arid, almost no plants
pt-ma-Pezj.summary: The eastern tip of the island is very dry with little or no vegetation.

pt-ma-TwjW.title: Plants: ferns everywhere
pt-ma-TwjW.summary: Ferns are very common across the island.

pt-ma-VNQl.title: Landscape: many tunnels
pt-ma-VNQl.summary: Because of the mountains, tunnels are very common.

pt-ma-WqRe.title: Landscape: low clouds
pt-ma-WqRe.summary: Low clouds are typical on the island and often show up in Street View.

pt-ma-kfwz.title: Sign: unique speed limit signs on highways
pt-ma-kfwz.summary: Special speed limit signs unique to Madeira on its highways.

pt-ma-nSn4.title: Plants: banana plantations in the south
pt-ma-nSn4.summary: Most banana plantations are in the south.

pt-ma-ooPx.title: Direction sign: striped signpost
pt-ma-ooPx.summary: Signposts are often striped, as on the Azores.

pt-ma-qA1O.title: Pole: mainland-style infrastructure on island
pt-ma-qA1O.summary: Madeira is an autonomous region, so poles and chevrons look like those on the mainland.

pt-ma-uInB.title: Guardrail: concrete block barriers
pt-ma-uInB.summary: Concrete block barriers, usually painted white, often line the roads.

pt-ma-uLdi.title: Bridge: dark green railings
pt-ma-uLdi.summary: Bridges often have dark green railings.

pt-ma-vS4A.title: Taxi: yellow with blue stripe
pt-ma-vS4A.summary: Taxis are yellow with a blue stripe along the sides.

pt-ma-yIaR.title: Sign: bus stop in black, white and yellow
pt-ma-yIaR.summary: Bus stop signs use a unique black, white and yellow colour scheme.

pt-oTO0.title: Phone numbers: first three digits show the region
pt-oTO0.summary: The first three digits of a landline are the area code, and they are spread out by region. Codes not starting with 2 are not regional, and codes starting with 29 are Azores or Madeira.

pt-pUNV.title: Sidewalk: bright cobblestones
pt-pUNV.summary: Cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common.

pt-rEuU.title: Plants: olive plantations in dense rows
pt-rEuU.summary: Olive plantations are more common in the eastern half, especially the far northeast and a bit of the southeast. Olives are planted in dense rows; the oaks of the previous tip are sparse with no pattern.

pt-sUvJ.title: Coverage: islands count as the mainland country
pt-sUvJ.summary: Madeira (southwest) and the Azores (west) both count as the same country for streak purposes.

pt-tuqy.title: Road: cobblestones set diagonally
pt-tuqy.summary: Cobblestone roads are very common, usually square stones laid diagonally to the road direction.

pt-x15t.title: Pedestrian sign: five stripes, high belt
pt-x15t.summary: Five stripes and a person wearing a noticeably high belt. Spanish signs have eight stripes, Italian figures have no belt, and Greek signs have two dotted lines instead of stripes.

differs.how: Greek signs have two dotted lines
